reasons: Includes its own tests showing the reader finds real constants and fails on missing ones.
Each comparison has a clear failure message that names the files to change.
Depends on text patterns, so it needs manual updates if the TypeScript style changes.

terms.meaning: a named value that does not change while the program runs
a rule of arithmetic that turns inputs into a result
a multiplier the value engine applies to a figure, based on how well the case is evidenced
the programming language the browser viewer is written in
the web page that displays records and results to a reader
a text pattern used to find matching text in a file
the test runner used for the Python tests

used_by: Run by pytest as part of the Python test suite; no other file imports it

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose and header
sections.what: Explains why the viewer copies some numbers and why this file exists to compare the copies. Sets the repository root path used to find the other files.
sections.why: The header records the incident that prompted the check and explains that a source read is the only way to compare two languages.
sections.watch_out: The pairs listed in the header and in the code must stay in step. If a pair is added, update both.

sections.name: typescript_number
sections.title: Reader for TypeScript numbers and the list of pairs
sections.what: Finds a line that declares a named number in a TypeScript file and returns its value, failing with a clear message if the name is missing. Also holds the list of three constant pairs to compare, each with its file, expected value, and Python name.
sections.why: Lets the test read the viewer's copied numbers without running JavaScript.
sections.watch_out: The pattern matches only a simple export line with a plain number. A declaration written in another style will look missing.

sections.name: python_value
sections.title: Reader for Python numbers
sections.what: Imports a Python module by its dotted name and returns the named value as a number.
sections.why: Lets the test compare the Python original with the TypeScript copy.
sections.watch_out: Importing a module runs its code, so a broken engine import fails this test with an error that may look unrelated.

sections.name: TestTheReaderWorks
sections.title: Checks that the reader itself works
sections.what: Confirms the TypeScript reader finds a real constant with a positive value, and raises an error for a name that does not exist.
sections.why: A reader that returned nothing would make every comparison look like agreement.
sections.watch_out: If this test fails, the comparison results cannot be trusted.

sections.name: TestEveryDuplicatedConstantAgrees
sections.title: Comparing each copied constant
sections.what: For each pair, checks that the TypeScript value equals the Python value and that both equal the value this test was written against. The failure messages name the likely cause, including that a deliberate change needs edits in three places.
sections.why: The purpose is to catch a copy that moved without its original.
sections.watch_out: A deliberate change must be made in the Python code, the TypeScript code, and this test together.

sections.name: TestTheWideningFormulaAgrees
sections.title: Checking the widening formula matches
sections.what: Reproduces the TypeScript widening formula in Python and compares the result with the real Python function at five confidence levels. A second check confirms the TypeScript function still contains the same expression.
sections.why: A formula can drift even when its constant does not, so the expression itself is checked as well.
sections.watch_out: The second check compares text with spaces removed. Any rewrite of the expression, even a correct one, fails and needs this test updated.

summary: Checks that three numbers and one formula copied from the Python engine into the TypeScript viewer still agree with the Python originals.
purpose: Stop a copied constant or formula from drifting between the Python engine and the TypeScript viewer, so the viewer never shows a figure the engine did not compute.
why: The module header records an incident where a changed floor value went unnoticed. The Python tests stayed green while a client-facing figure in the viewer was wrong.
how: Reads the TypeScript source as plain text, finds each named constant with a text pattern, and reads the Python value by importing its module. Compares each pair. Then reproduces the widening formula in Python and compares it with the real function at five confidence levels. Finally checks that the TypeScript function body still contains the matching expression.
inputs: A fixed list of constant pairs, with file paths and expected values, defined in the module. The TypeScript source files and the Python modules they copy from.
outputs: Pytest pass or fail. Failures show the two mismatched values, the file involved, and a hint about which places to edit.
risks: Reading TypeScript with a text pattern can miss a constant written in a different style. The formula check matches text with spaces removed, so a correct rewrite of the expression would fail. A new copied constant must be added to the list by hand.
debug: If a test says the constant is not declared, check the spelling and the export line in the TypeScript file. If two values differ, check both sides and the expected value in this file. If the formula check fails after an edit, compare the expression text with the one this test expects.
